target: Same-day SNMF-reported incident near a route-sector center within 20 km; a regional report proxy, not physical fire presence or ignition probability.

protocol.model: StandardScaler + route one-hot + class-balanced logistic regression, C=1, random_state=42.
protocol.threshold_selection: None; these are diagnostic comparisons on the held-out year.
protocol.label_reconstruction: Archived SNMF report parser logic, including active/unresolved same-day listings and reported start dates; zeros only on dates with an archived daily report.
protocol.label_reconstruction_check: Reconstructed 20 km route-day and positive counts must equal the pre-existing 2023/2024 route-proxy audits before training proceeds.

explicit_no_fire_negative_challenge.target: SNMF explicitly states no fires were reported nationally on the report date; administrative proxy only.

interpretation: At 20 km, ranking improves over the route-day prevalence baseline, but raw scores are poorly calibrated: the Brier score is much worse than the constant-prevalence baseline.
At threshold 0.5 the model detects 35/52 positive report-proxy route-days but emits 566 alerts on route-days without a nearby listed incident.
At threshold 0.9 only 2/52 positive route-days are detected; this remains an exploratory test on a broad, report-derived regional target.
The 20 km sensitivity radius expands beyond immediate route exposure and still does not yield a dependable operating threshold.
limitations: No nearby reported incident is not verified physical absence; only the explicit no-fire challenge dates provide the stronger administrative negative proxy.
Route-sector centers are used instead of complete trail polylines; 20 km describes regional proximity rather than on-trail exposure.
The full 2024 test contains only 52 positive route-days, many repeated across event episodes.
Diagnostic thresholds were not selected on a separate validation period.
Weather forecasts omit fuels, ignition likelihood, satellite observability, and local operational closures.
